scenario: Patient with mild OSA (AHI 6) requests split-night PSG after failed HSAT showing technically inadequate results due to probe dislodgement. Provider orders facility-based PSG citing HSAT failure.
complexity: HSAT failure pathway vs AHI threshold
expected: APPROVE (split-night PSG)
tricky: Agent may incorrectly deny based on mild AHI, but LCD allows facility PSG when HSAT is technically inadequate regardless of AHI.

scenario: Pediatric patient (age 5) with suspected OSA. Provider orders unattended home sleep test (HSAT Type III). No prior in-lab PSG.
expected: DENY (HSAT not validated for pediatrics)
tricky: Agent must know HSAT is not validated/covered for children; in-lab PSG is required. Easy to miss age-based exclusion.

scenario: Patient has comorbid CHF (NYHA III) and suspected OSA. Provider orders HSAT instead of in-lab PSG.
expected: DENY (HSAT inappropriate for significant cardiopulmonary disease)
tricky: LCD excludes HSAT for patients with significant cardiopulmonary disease. Agent must flag CHF as disqualifying for home testing.

scenario: Patient diagnosed with narcolepsy via clinical history only. Provider requests MSLT without preceding overnight PSG.
expected: DENY (MSLT requires preceding nocturnal PSG)
tricky: MSLT is only covered when preceded by overnight PSG to rule out other sleep disorders. Agent may approve MSLT in isolation.

scenario: Repeat PSG requested 8 weeks after initial diagnostic PSG for OSA, with no intervening treatment trial. Reason: 'Patient wants second opinion.'
expected: DENY (no clinical indication for repeat)
tricky: No treatment attempted, no clinical change. LCD requires medical necessity for repeat studies. Agent may approve if it doesn't check for prior studies.

scenario: Patient with severe OSA (AHI 38) requests oral appliance as first-line treatment. No CPAP trial documented.
expected: CONDITIONAL — depends on LCD
tricky: Some LCDs require CPAP trial/failure before oral appliance for severe OSA; others allow physician discretion. Agent must check jurisdiction-specific rules.

scenario: Patient requests replacement oral appliance (E0486) after 2 years. Original device is functional but patient reports discomfort. No clinical re-evaluation documented.
expected: DENY (no documented clinical re-evaluation or device failure)
tricky: Replacement requires documented device failure, clinical re-evaluation, or change in dental/skeletal anatomy. Comfort alone is insufficient.

scenario: Dentist (not physician) orders oral appliance for OSA. Sleep study was performed and interpreted by the dentist's affiliated sleep lab. No independent physician involvement.
expected: DENY (requires physician order and diagnosis)
tricky: OSA diagnosis and oral appliance prescription must involve a physician. A dentist can fabricate/fit but cannot independently order DME for Medicare.

scenario: Patient with central sleep apnea (not obstructive) requests oral appliance E0486. AHI 22, all central events.
expected: DENY (oral appliances only covered for OSA)
tricky: LCD specifically covers obstructive sleep apnea. Central apnea is a different pathophysiology not addressed by mandibular advancement.

scenario: Oral appliance billed with E0485 (prefabricated) but documentation describes custom impressions, bite registration, and lab fabrication.
expected: FLAG/DENY (should be E0486 custom, not E0485 prefab)
tricky: Agent must detect CPT/HCPCS code mismatch with clinical documentation. Upcoding or downcoding issue.

scenario: Patient prescribed BiPAP (E0470) for OSA with AHI 18. No documented CPAP failure. Provider states patient 'prefers BiPAP.'
expected: DENY (BiPAP requires documented CPAP failure for OSA)
tricky: BiPAP for OSA requires prior CPAP trial failure. Patient preference alone doesn't meet medical necessity. Agent may miss step-therapy requirement.

scenario: CPAP compliance download shows 3.2 hours average use over 90 days. Provider requests continued CPAP rental beyond initial period citing 'patient is trying.'
expected: DENY (does not meet 4hr/night ≥70% of nights compliance)
tricky: Medicare requires ≥4 hours/night on ≥70% of nights in a 30-day period during initial 90 days. 3.2 avg fails. Agent may approve based on partial compliance.

scenario: Patient with obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS) and concurrent OSA. Provider orders ASV (adaptive servo-ventilation) device.
expected: REQUIRES CAREFUL REVIEW — ASV contraindicated if predominant central apnea with EF<45%
tricky: ASV has a safety contraindication for certain heart failure patients. Agent must check ejection fraction and central vs obstructive pattern.

scenario: Patient with Stage 2 pressure ulcer requests negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT). Wound is 4cm², clean, no infection.
expected: DENY (Stage 2 does not meet NPWT criteria)
tricky: NPWT typically requires Stage 3/4 or full-thickness wounds that have failed prior treatment. Stage 2 is too superficial. Agent may approve based on wound presence alone.

scenario: Provider applies two different skin substitute products to the same wound on the same date of service. Bills for both.
expected: DENY one of the two (cannot stack skin substitutes on same wound same DOS)
tricky: LCDs prohibit applying multiple skin substitutes to same wound on same date. Agent must detect duplicate/stacked billing.

scenario: 81479 (unlisted molecular pathology) billed for a 90-gene pharmacogenomic panel on a patient with no current medication management issues. Ordered 'prophylactically.'
expected: DENY (no current clinical indication)
tricky: LCD requires active medication management problem. Prophylactic pharmacogenomic testing is not covered. Agent may approve based on the perceived sophistication of the test.

scenario: Whole exome sequencing ordered for a patient after a single-gene test was negative. No documentation of genetic counseling or prior targeted panel.
expected: DENY or REQUEST MORE INFO (many LCDs require targeted panels before WES)
tricky: Exome sequencing often requires documented failure of targeted/panel testing first. Agent must enforce tiered testing approach.

scenario: Lumbar MRI requested for acute low back pain of 2 weeks duration. No red flags, no neurological deficits, no prior conservative treatment.
expected: DENY (conservative treatment ≥6 weeks required first)
tricky: LCD and NCD require 6+ weeks of conservative therapy before advanced imaging for uncomplicated LBP. Agent may approve due to patient pain complaints.

scenario: PET scan requested for initial staging of a newly diagnosed small (T1a) renal cell carcinoma. No metastatic symptoms.
expected: DENY (PET not indicated for initial staging of small RCC)
tricky: PET is not covered for initial staging of renal cell carcinoma per NCD. Agent must know cancer-specific PET indications rather than applying a blanket 'cancer = PET approved' rule.

scenario: Cardiac MRI requested for a patient with chronic stable chest pain, normal stress test, normal echo, and normal coronary CTA performed 3 months ago.
expected: DENY (no incremental diagnostic value after comprehensive negative workup)
tricky: Multiple prior negative studies make cardiac MRI medically unnecessary. Agent must evaluate cumulative prior workup, not just the single request.

scenario: Patient with BMI 33 and type 2 diabetes requests Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Documents show 4 months of supervised weight management (LCD requires 6 months).
expected: DENY (does not meet 6-month supervised diet requirement)
tricky: BMI 33 with comorbidity can qualify, but 6 months of documented supervised nutrition is mandatory. 4 months is insufficient. Agent may round up or miss the duration check.

scenario: Lumbar fusion (single level) requested for degenerative disc disease. MRI shows disc desiccation at L4-L5 but no instability, no spondylolisthesis, no stenosis causing radiculopathy. Conservative care: 3 months PT only.
expected: DENY (does not meet fusion criteria — no instability, insufficient conservative care)
tricky: Fusion for DDD typically requires instability or failed ≥6 months conservative care with radiculopathy. Imaging finding alone insufficient.

scenario: Dupixent (dupilumab) requested for atopic dermatitis. Patient tried topical steroids for 2 weeks and one systemic immunosuppressant for 3 weeks. LCD requires 'adequate trial' of each.
expected: DENY (trials too short — typically ≥3 months topical, ≥3 months systemic)
tricky: Agent must know what constitutes an 'adequate trial' — brief exposures don't count. Specific duration thresholds vary by LCD but 2-3 weeks is universally insufficient.

scenario: Ozempic (semaglutide) prescribed for weight loss in a patient with BMI 28, no diabetes, no cardiovascular disease. Provider codes it as diabetes management but A1c is 5.2%.
expected: DENY (fraudulent diagnosis coding; BMI <30 without comorbidity doesn't qualify for weight indication either)
tricky: Agent must cross-reference the billed diagnosis against clinical data. A1c 5.2% contradicts diabetes diagnosis. This tests fraud detection capability.

scenario: Patient resides in Puerto Rico. Provider submits oral appliance claim to Noridian (J-D DME MAC). The applicable LCD is from CGS Administrators (J-C, which covers Puerto Rico for DME).
expected: FLAG — wrong MAC jurisdiction
tricky: Puerto Rico DME goes through CGS (J-C per L33611), not Noridian. Agent must validate correct jurisdictional assignment before applying LCD criteria.

scenario: Prior auth submitted 3 days AFTER the oral appliance was delivered and fitted. Provider claims 'urgent medical necessity' but documentation shows routine scheduling.
expected: DENY (retroactive PA not permitted for non-emergent DME)
tricky: Most MACs deny retroactive PA for elective DME. Agent may incorrectly approve if it doesn't check service date vs auth request date.

scenario: Patient with OSA and chronic insomnia. Provider orders both PSG (covered under L33405) and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia device (not covered under any LCD). Single combined claim submitted.
expected: PARTIAL APPROVE — approve PSG, deny CBT-I device
tricky: Agent must parse a single claim with items falling under different coverage rules. Cannot blanket approve/deny the entire claim.

scenario: Patient has both OSA (AHI 12) and restless leg syndrome. Provider orders PSG + MSLT + actigraphy all on the same authorization. Actigraphy was removed from LCD coverage in R9 revision (07/01/2020).
expected: APPROVE PSG, DENY MSLT (no narcolepsy indication), DENY actigraphy (removed from coverage)
tricky: Agent must track LCD revision history — actigraphy was explicitly removed in the R9 revision. Also must evaluate MSLT indication independently.

scenario: CPAP authorization request includes sleep study results showing AHI 32, but the sleep study was performed at a non-accredited facility with no documentation of technologist credentials. LCD requires accredited facility or qualified personnel.
expected: DENY or REQUEST MORE INFO (facility accreditation/personnel credentials not documented)
tricky: Agent must verify not just clinical results but also the qualifications of the testing facility and personnel. Easy to approve based on AHI alone.

scenario: Oral appliance PA submitted with a valid sleep study showing AHI 15, physician order, and diagnosis of OSA — but the sleep study is dated 4 years ago. No recent clinical re-evaluation. Patient's weight has changed by +40 lbs since the study.
expected: DENY or REQUEST UPDATED STUDY (clinical status has materially changed)
tricky: A 4-year-old sleep study with significant weight change may no longer reflect current disease severity. Agent must evaluate temporal validity of supporting documentation.
